title: Real-Time Chat System
summary: Deliver messages the instant they're sent, with presence and durable history, across a fleet of servers.
narrative:
Chat is fundamentally bidirectional. The server can't wait for a client to poll — the moment a message arrives it has to be pushed to the recipient. That rules out plain request/response and calls for persistent connections: WebSockets that stay open so either side can send at any time.

The hard part is that a million users don't all land on the same server. When Alice, connected to server A, messages Bob, connected to server B, server A has to get that message across to server B. A Pub/Sub layer solves this: each server subscribes to the channels for the users it holds, and any server can publish to fan a message out to whichever server owns the recipient. A cache tracks presence — who is online and which server currently holds their connection — so routing stays fast.

Messages also have to survive. History must be durable and readable later, but writing to storage can't slow delivery. So push each message onto a queue and persist it to a NoSQL store off the hot path. Delivery stays instant; history is written reliably in the background. Build the fleet, wire the fan-out, and keep persistence asynchronous.

functional: Deliver messages in real time over persistent connections
Fan a message out to a recipient on any server
Track who is online and where they're connected
nonFunctional: Message delivery under 150 ms at p99
No messages dropped, even across server restarts
Survive the loss of any single WebSocket server
constraints: Clients connect only through the load balancer
History is written off the delivery hot path
specs.tradeoff: Pushing history through a queue trades write-time immediacy for fast, reliable delivery and durable storage that never blocks a send.
specs.bonus: Add Monitoring to track connection counts, fan-out lag, and queue depth.

missions.label: Connect clients through the Load Balancer
Route connections to a WebSocket Server
Fan messages out across servers via Pub/Sub
Track presence and connection routing in the Cache
Persist message history to the NoSQL store

topologyRules.message: Connections must enter through the Load Balancer, not straight to a WebSocket server.
Clients must never read the history store directly.
History access must go through the WebSocket tier and its persistence pipeline.

resilienceRules.message: Run at least two WebSocket servers so a single failure doesn't drop every open connection.
Cross-server delivery needs Pub/Sub to fan messages out to whichever server holds the recipient.

hints: Clients hold a persistent connection: Client → Load Balancer → WebSocket Server. Run at least two WebSocket servers so no single failure disconnects everyone.
Connect the WebSocket servers to Pub/Sub so a message from one server reaches a recipient on any other, and use the Cache for presence and connection routing.
Don't write history on the delivery path — push messages onto the Message Queue and persist them to the NoSQL store from there.
